title: Soft point-contact Andreev reflection spectroscopy in a palm-type cubic anvil-pressure cell
authors: Qingxin Dong, Fengrui Shi, Yan Zhang, Tong Shi, Yi Liu, Shaoheng Ruan, Zhongjin Wu, Jianping Sun, Zhaoming Tian, Yoshiya Uwatoko, Guanghan Cao, Xin Lu, Bosen Wang, Jin-Guang Cheng
abstract: We have implemented soft point-contact Andreev reflection spectroscopy (PCARS) in a palm-type cubic anvil pressure cell by combining a substrate anchoring strategy with an external wire-splitting technique. This design enables the stable formation of multiple point contact junctions under hydrostatic pressures up to 15 GPa. Benchmark measurements on the elemental superconductor Nb demonstrate high reproducibility and yield a zero-temperature superconducting gap with a gap ratio of 3.3. We further apply this technique to the Kagome metal superconductor CsCr3Sb5 and the bilayer nickelate superconductor La2PrNi2O7. Pronounced zero-bias conductance peaks are observed, and their evolution with temperature, magnetic field and applied pressure is investigated, together with the superconducting gap magnitude and possible pairing symmetries. These measurements provide spectroscopic evidence consistent with unconventional superconductivity in these materials. Our work establishes a robust experimental platform that bridges macroscopic electrical transport and microscopic spectroscopic probes, opening a new avenue for investigating pairing symmetry in a wide range of pressure-induced unconventional superconductors.
summary: This work introduces a novel and robust experimental platform—soft point-contact Andreev reflection spectroscopy (PCARS)—to measure superconducting gaps under ultra-high hydrostatic pressure. By testing this technique on various superconductors, the authors provide spectroscopic evidence suggesting unconventional pairing symmetries in materials like $	ext{CsCr}_3	ext{Sb}_5$ and $	ext{La}_2	ext{PrNi}_2	ext{O}_7$. This advances the field by bridging macroscopic transport measurements with microscopic quantum characterization under extreme conditions.
main_problem: The primary goal is to overcome the scarcity of reliable probes that can access microscopic superconducting-state properties, such as pairing symmetry, in materials under extreme high pressures.
main_result: The authors successfully established a robust experimental platform using soft point-contact Andreev reflection spectroscopy (PCARS) in a cubic anvil cell, providing spectroscopic evidence consistent with unconventional superconductivity in pressure-induced superconductors like CsCr3Sb5 and La2PrNi2O7.
method: They employed PCARS by measuring the differential conductance (dI/dV) of normal-metal-superconductor junctions under hydrostatic pressures up to 15 GPa, utilizing a specialized substrate anchoring and wire-splitting technique.
model_or_system: The study investigates elemental superconductors (Nb) and complex oxides/chalcogenides ($	ext{CsCr}_3	ext{Sb}_5$, $	ext{La}_2	ext{PrNi}_2	ext{O}_7$) as systems exhibiting superconductivity. The analysis involves fitting the measured spectra using theoretical models for different pairing symmetries (e.g., isotropic s-wave vs. d-wave).
key_observables: Superconducting gap magnitude ($\Delta$), zero-bias conductance peaks (ZBCP), and the ratio $2\Delta(0)/k_B T_c$.
important_parameters: Hydrostatic pressure ($P$) up to 15 GPa, temperature ($T$), and applied magnetic field ($H$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting the spectra using specific theoretical models (s-wave or d-wave) and assumes that observed features are not solely due to extrinsic contact resistance effects.
figures_summary: Figures detail the setup in a CAC, showing $R(T)$ vs. pressure for multiple materials ($	ext{Nb}$, $	ext{CsCr}_3	ext{Sb}_5$, $	ext{La}_2	ext{PrNi}_2	ext{O}_7$), and presenting corresponding Andreev spectra ($dI/dV$) analyzed using theoretical fitting models.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the advanced experimental setup (PCARS in CAC), validates it with a benchmark material ($	ext{Nb}$), and then applies this robust technique sequentially to two different unconventional superconductors ($	ext{CsCr}_3	ext{Sb}_5$ and $	ext{La}_2	ext{PrNi}_2	ext{O}_7$) to characterize their superconducting gaps under pressure.
why_interesting: The ability to probe microscopic pairing symmetries (d-wave vs. s-wave) in strongly correlated materials like nickelates or kagome metals, while simultaneously applying extreme pressures, provides crucial data for understanding high-$T_c$ mechanisms relevant to condensed matter theory.
